name: Putnam County, NY
findings: Putnam County has 324 nonprofit organizations. 143 of them (44%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 120 organizations.
Social and fraternal organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (24% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Putnam County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.

observations.title: Few religious organizations list membership
observations.text: 5 religious organizations here list membership. In similar places of this size, about 15 would.

confidence.text: Based on 15 organizations here; 39% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Do people here look for groups to join through religious groups? Where else does that happen?

observations.title: More organizations list civic or political action
observations.text: Per resident, more organizations in Putnam County list civic or political action in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 1.7 times the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 10 organizations here; 39% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Why are ways to take civic or political action so common here? Who takes part, and who might not be reached?

observations.title: Foundation organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 14 foundation organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.

confidence.text: Based on 14 organizations here; 39% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: What do foundation organizations here do in the community? How do people find out about them?
